title: Bind SCHC fragmentation contexts and tombstones to key generation
description: Security review found an identity-domain mismatch across the updated specs. draft-lichen-link-01 §4.3 says both replay and SCHC fragmentation state use (SignerPublicKey, KeyGeneration), but spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6 and draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 §5 key active contexts/tombstones only by local/full remote signer identities plus directional Rule ID. A trust-store generation can change while the same public key/EUI alias is reinstalled, so keying only by public-key identity can let a new generation inherit or collide with retired-generation partial reassembly/tombstone state. Make the opaque current key-generation token an explicit component of remote fragmentation ownership (and local generation where relevant), require current-generation revalidation before mutation/control responses, invalidate retired generations atomically, and add vectors/tests for revoke/reinstall of the same public key.
notes: Rust complete: opaque runtime and durable trust-generation identities propagate from authenticated link evidence through peer authority, permits, active sessions, tombstones, and persisted floors. Same-key revoke/reinstall retires old capability and atomically isolates state. Full link/SCHC/node tests, clippy, fmt, and no-default checks pass.
